evidence: Receiving DO2 fell from 10.38 mg/L at 50.0h to 1.80 mg/L at 50.2h and stayed 1.24–1.90 mg/L through 52.0h — below the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Receiving P assays: 1.09 g/L @36h, 3.04 g/L @48h — mid-growth, matching source trajectory to ~8 g/L peak at 72h
Physical forward model (source-calibrated): estimated transfer multiplier ≈0.40 at h≈50, indicating an oxygen-transfer capacity loss event

Model comparison: strong_feed_reduction gives min DO 0.87 mg/L, post-decision deficit 7.95 mg·h/L, product mass 194.0 kg — best across all actions; keep yields 0.80/8.40/193.9; increase_air 0.71/12.3; combined 0.77/10.6
Model sensitivity: 0/5 feasible members for every action, with strong_feed_reduction min-DO range 0.45–1.29 mg/L
args.rationale: The receiving batch suffered a step DO2 collapse at ~50.2 h (10.4 → 1.2–1.9 mg/L), violating the 2.0 mg/L oxygen minimum while product was still in strong growth (3.04 g/L at 48h, on track toward the source-like ~8 g/L peak). A stop would forfeit all counted production. The nominal source-calibrated model attributes the deficit primarily to an oxygen-transfer capacity loss (multiplier ≈0.4), so supply-side increases (+15% air) cannot restore feasibility and even extend below-limit exposure. Demand-side reduction is the only lever that mitigates the deficit, and the strongest bounded feed cut (0.6×) performs best: lowest post-decision oxygen deficit (7.95 vs 8.40 mg·h/L under keep), highest predicted minimum DO, and the highest retained product mass (~194 kg). I therefore recommend strong_feed_reduction. Caveat: the model is imperfect and source-calibrated, not the hidden truth; its sensitivity analysis shows no action fully restores DO above 2.0 mg/L, so close monitoring and escalation (equipment transfer-capacity investigation) remain warranted.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated, not the hidden receiving realization; predicted DO2 remains below the 2.0 mg/L limit for all actions (0/5 feasible sensitivity members), so the intervention mitigates but may not eliminate the constraint violation. Delayed assay information (next P point at ~52h available at 56h) could revise trajectory estimates. The true root cause (transfer-capacity loss vs. contamination event) is inferred from the DO2 step at 50.2h and is not directly observed.
